subject: LlamaIndex runtime hooks: certification criteria and sandbox access
messages:
From: Amit Kaur <amit@sagebridge.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Li <nora@llamaindex.org>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LlamaIndex runtime hooks: certification request

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. We're ready to move our LlamaIndex instrumentation through Redwood's partner sandbox so we can validate runtime hook compatibility (KV cache handling + async trace propagation). Nora from LlamaIndex is looped in to confirm the hook points.

Can you share the acceptance checklist your integrations team uses, as well as instructions for creating a sandbox tenant and any transient credentials? We want to run a quick smoke test next week and capture token/batch-level telemetry to ensure no regressions on the UTF-8 tokenization edge cases we've been seeing.

High-level asks: 
- acceptance criteria matrix (what passes/fails)
- test account + dataset size recommendations
- expected timeline for certification (approx days)

Attaching our internal runbook (light) for context. Happy to sync if that's easier.

Best,
Amit
Head of Integrations, SageBridge Labs
attachments: sb_runbook_v0.9.md (text)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Kaur <amit@sagebridge.ai>
Cc: Nora Li <nora@llamaindex.org>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LlamaIndex runtime hooks: certification request

Amit —

Thanks for the context and the runbook. I've attached our acceptance checklist (llamaindex_acceptance_checklist_v1.xlsx) and the sandbox on‑boarding PDF with step‑by‑step keys (sandbox-access-instructions.pdf). Quick notes:

- The checklist is split into Functional, Observability, and Performance gates. The observability gate will require a short trace sample with KV cache TTLs and a token attribution sample.
- For your smoke test, create a sandbox tenant with a single small GPU instance (g4dn-like) and a dataset of ~250–500 short docs (under 2k tokens) to exercise prefix/KV caching.
- Expect ~3 business days for the first pass (engineer validation + one replay). Full certification (including regression set) is typically 7–10 business days if no outstanding failures.

Next steps I propose:
1) You provision the tenant using step 1 in the PDF and send admin@redwood a request (we'll provision a temporary API key).
2) Vanessa will coordinate the acceptance run and run the observability checks.
3) Nora, if you can provide a short snippet of the runtime hook we should expect (the signature + sample payload), we can pre-wire the tracer.

I'll set up a Slack channel for faster triage.

—Rishi
Senior Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | https://redwood.ai
attachments: llamaindex_acceptance_checklist_v1.xlsx, sandbox-access-instructions.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LlamaIndex runtime hooks: certification request

Amit / Nora —

Quick clarification from the ops side: when you request the tenant, please indicate whether you want persistent logs retained for 30 days or 90 days. For the acceptance run we recommend 30 days (keeps cost down). If you expect a longer investigation window (e.g., legal/evidence), pick 90.

Also: to avoid tokenization noise, please include a small set of unit prompts that include newlines, emojis, and mixed encodings — we've seen differences between tokenizer versions that matter for prefix caching.

I'll own the acceptance run scheduling once you confirm tenant + retention. Propose Wed/Thu next week for the smoke test.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Programs, Redwood Inference
From: Amit Kaur <amit@sagebridge.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Li <nora@llamaindex.org>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LlamaIndex runtime hooks: certification request

Thanks — 30 days retention is fine for now. We'll spin up the tenant today and request the temporary API key using the support flow in the PDF. Nora — attaching the runtime hook snippet we expect; it includes the async context id and the kv_cache_id.

Also, can you confirm the format you need for the trace sample? JSONL with a single event per line, or a zipped trace bundle? We can produce both but want to send the one that reduces back-and-forth.

I'll ping in the Slack channel once the tenant is created.

—Amit
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Kaur <amit@sagebridge.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LlamaIndex runtime hooks: certification request

All —

Thanks for the quick movement. For the trace sample, please send JSONL (one event per line) and attach a short README that maps the fields we should expect. That format plugs straight into our ingestion pipeline and speeds validation.

I'll add this to the partner sprint board and tag the acceptance tickets: SB-7421-ACPT and SB-7421-OBS. If anything blocks the tenant provisioning, loop in infra-support@redwood.ai and mention the DEAL-7421-SB id.

See you on Slack.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of ISV Partnerships, Redwood Inference
